verses.1: Indeed, when spoken to thus by Valmiki, Rama, having seen Sita of excellent complexion in the midst of the people, replied with folded hands.
verses.2: O great fortunate one, O knower of dharma, this is indeed as you say, and my conviction is established by your pure words, O Brahmana.
verses.3: Although Vaidehi's purity was previously proven by an oath taken in the presence of the gods, and she was admitted back into the home, the powerful public scandal compelled me to abandon Maithili.
verses.4: O Brahman, knowing her to be sinless, I abandoned Sita out of fear of public opinion, and for this, you should forgive me.
verses.5: I know that these two, Kusha and Lava, are my twin sons, and I desire that my affection for Maithili, who is pure in the eyes of the world, be restored.
verses.6: Having understood Rama's intention regarding Sita's oath, the greatly powerful best among gods, led by Mahendra (Indra), prepared to act.
verses.7: All of them, indeed, assembled, making Grandfather Brahma their leader.
verses.8: The Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, the two Ashvins along with the Maruts, Gandharvas, and Apsaras, all indeed had assembled there.
verses.9: The Sadhyas, Vishvedevas, all great sages, Nagas, Suparnas, and Siddhas, all of them with joyful minds, agitated by Sita's oath, had indeed assembled there.
verses.10: Having seen the gods and sages, Rama spoke again, saying, "O best among men, I have conviction in the faultless words of the sages."
verses.11: Let my affection for Vaidehi, who is pure in the midst of the world, be firm.
verses.12: Then, the auspicious, sacred, divinely fragrant, and delightful wind, the best among gods (Vayu), delighted that multitude of people from all sides.
verses.13: People gathered from all kingdoms beheld that wonderful and inconceivable sight, just as they would have in the Krita Yuga.
verses.14: Having seen all the assembled people, Sita, clad in ochre robes, spoke with folded hands, her eyes and face cast downwards.
verses.15: Sita prayed, "Just as I do not think of any other man than Rama even in my mind, so may Goddess Earth grant me an opening."
verses.16: Sita prayed, "Just as I worship Rama with my mind, actions, and speech, so may Goddess Earth grant me an opening."
verses.17: Sita prayed, "Just as this truth has been spoken by me and I know no one superior to Rama, so may Goddess Earth grant me an opening."
verses.18: As Vaidehi was thus swearing, a wonderful, divine, and unsurpassed throne emerged from the surface of the earth.
verses.19: This divine throne was being held by the heads of Nagas of immeasurable valor, who themselves possessed divine bodies adorned with divine jewels.
verses.20: Then, Goddess Earth, taking Maithili with her two arms, greeted her with a welcome and made her sit upon that throne.
verses.21: As Sita, seated on the throne, was seen entering the netherworld, an uninterrupted divine shower of flowers fell upon her.
verses.22: A very great acclamation of "well done" suddenly arose from the gods, praising, "Well done, well done, O Sita, whose character is indeed of such purity!"
verses.23: The celestial gods, with joyful minds, uttered various words upon witnessing Sita's entry into the earth.
verses.24: All those sages and kings, who were like tigers among men, present in the sacrificial enclosure, did not cease their astonishment.
verses.25: All stationary and moving beings in the sky and on the earth, along with the huge-bodied demons and the lords of serpents in the netherworld, were present.
verses.26: Some, greatly delighted, roared; some were absorbed in meditation; some gazed at Rama, while others, stunned, looked at Sita.
verses.27: Upon witnessing Sita's entry, there was a great gathering of beings, and for a moment, the entire world seemed exceedingly bewildered. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तनवतितमः सर्गः ।। 97 ।। Thus ends the ninety-seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
